```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 96
)
```

[reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/) makes sortable, searchable
tables for the web, and [reactablefmtr](https://kcuilla.github.io/reactablefmtr/)
adds ready-made cell formats on top of it: data bars, color tiles, icon sets,
pill buttons, merged columns, embedded images and table themes. sdvplotR's
`reactable_sdv_*()` helpers supply the team side: logos, wordmarks, headshots
and team colors, resolved from the same team keys as the rest of the package.
Recipes 1 to 6 combine the two packages; recipes 7 to 10 use reactable alone
for things the [reactable integration](reactable-integration.html) article does
not show.

reactablefmtr is not an sdvplotR dependency. Install it from GitHub:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("kcuilla/reactablefmtr")
```

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(reactable)
library(reactablefmtr)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
```

Every table below is one row per team or player, aggregated from the season's
box scores or schedules, so a page embeds a few kilobytes of data rather than
the play-by-play.

## 1. NBA: data bars in each team's color

`data_bars()` draws a bar in each cell, and `fill_color_ref` names a column
that holds each row's bar color. `sdv_team_colors()` fills that column with
each team's primary color, so the bars carry the same colors as the logos.
The color column is hidden with `show = FALSE`.

```{r nba-data}
nba_box <- hoopR::load_nba_team_box(2026) |>
  filter(season_type == 2)

nba <- nba_box |>
  group_by(team = team_abbreviation, team_id) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    wins = sum(team_score > opponent_team_score),
    ppg = mean(team_score),
    opp_ppg = mean(opponent_team_score),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # drops the All-Star games; the NBA Cup final, which the standings do not
  # count, stays in the two finalists' lines
  filter(games >= 70) |>
  mutate(margin = ppg - opp_ppg, color = sdv_team_colors("nba", team)) |>
  arrange(desc(margin))
stopifnot(nrow(nba) == 30)
```

```{r nba-bars}
reactable(
  select(nba, team, wins, ppg, opp_ppg, margin, color),
  defaultPageSize = 10,
  columns = list(
    team = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "nba", height = 26), html = TRUE, width = 60),
    wins = colDef(name = "W", width = 60),
    ppg = colDef(name = "PPG", format = colFormat(digits = 1), width = 70),
    opp_ppg = colDef(name = "Opp PPG", format = colFormat(digits = 1), width = 80),
    margin = colDef(
      name = "Point margin per game",
      cell = data_bars(nba, fill_color_ref = "color", number_fmt = scales::label_number(0.1, style_positive = "plus"))
    ),
    color = colDef(show = FALSE)
  )
)
```

A team with a negative margin gets a bar to the left of the zero line, so the
table splits into winners and losers at a glance.

## 2. WNBA: a heatmap of team stats with `color_tiles()`

`color_tiles()` fills each cell by its value in the column, the same scale for
every row. Pass it the column's colors from low to high; turnovers and points
allowed get the reversed scale, so green always means better. The team column
uses `reactable_sdv_logos()`.

```{r wnba-tiles}
wnba <- wehoop::load_wnba_team_box(2025) |>
  filter(season_type == 2) |>
  group_by(team = team_abbreviation) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    pts = mean(team_score),
    opp_pts = mean(opponent_team_score),
    fg_pct = sum(field_goals_made) / sum(field_goals_attempted),
    fg3_pct = sum(three_point_field_goals_made) / sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted),
    reb = mean(total_rebounds),
    ast = mean(assists),
    tov = mean(turnovers),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(games >= 20) |> # drops the All-Star teams' single game
  arrange(desc(pts - opp_pts)) |>
  select(-games)

good <- c("#d7301f", "#fdf6e3", "#1a9850") # low to high, high is good
bad <- rev(good)
pct <- colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1)
num <- scales::label_number(0.1)

reactable(
  wnba,
  pagination = FALSE,
  defaultColDef = colDef(width = 72),
  columns = list(
    team = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "wnba", height = 26), html = TRUE, width = 60),
    pts = colDef(name = "PTS", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = good, number_fmt = num)),
    opp_pts = colDef(name = "OPP", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = bad, number_fmt = num)),
    fg_pct = colDef(name = "FG%", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = good, number_fmt = scales::label_percent(0.1))),
    fg3_pct = colDef(name = "3P%", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = good, number_fmt = scales::label_percent(0.1))),
    reb = colDef(name = "REB", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = good, number_fmt = num)),
    ast = colDef(name = "AST", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = good, number_fmt = num)),
    tov = colDef(name = "TOV", cell = color_tiles(wnba, colors = bad, number_fmt = num))
  )
)
```

## 3. NFL: player, team and headshot in one cell row with `merge_column()`

`merge_column()` writes a second column's value under (or beside) the cell's
own, so the quarterback's team abbreviation sits in small grey type under his
name and the table needs one column fewer. The headshot comes from
`reactable_sdv_headshots()`, which reads nflverse's GSIS ids, and the logo from
`reactable_sdv_logos()`.

```{r nfl-qbs}
qbs <- nflreadr::load_player_stats(2025, summary_level = "reg") |>
  filter(position == "QB", attempts >= 250) |>
  transmute(
    player_id, player = player_display_name, team = recent_team, logo = recent_team,
    games, attempts,
    epa_per_play = passing_epa / (attempts + sacks_suffered),
    cpoe = passing_cpoe,
    td = passing_tds, int = passing_interceptions
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(epa_per_play))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(qbs$player_id))

reactable(
  qbs,
  defaultPageSize = 12,
  columns = list(
    player_id = colDef(
      name = "", width = 60, html = TRUE,
      cell = reactable_sdv_headshots(league = "nfl", id_system = "gsis", height = 40)
    ),
    player = colDef(name = "Quarterback", minWidth = 160, cell = merge_column(qbs, merged_name = "team", merged_position = "below")),
    team = colDef(show = FALSE),
    logo = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "nfl", height = 28), html = TRUE, width = 56),
    games = colDef(name = "G", width = 50),
    attempts = colDef(name = "Att", width = 60),
    epa_per_play = colDef(name = "EPA/play", format = colFormat(digits = 3), width = 90),
    cpoe = colDef(name = "CPOE", format = colFormat(digits = 1), width = 70),
    td = colDef(name = "TD", width = 50),
    int = colDef(name = "INT", width = 50)
  )
)
```

## 4. MLB: run differential with `icon_sets()` and division `pill_buttons()`

`icon_sets()` puts an icon before each number, picked by the value's third of
the column: an up arrow for the best third, a dash for the middle and a down
arrow for the worst. `pill_buttons()` turns a text column into a rounded tag;
`color_ref` points at a column of colors, here each team's primary color, so
the tag reads as the team's.

```{r mlb-data}
mlb_clubs <- baseballr::mlb_teams(season = 2025, sport_ids = 1) |>
  select(team_id, team = team_abbreviation, division = division_name, venue_id)

mlb_standings <- baseballr::mlb_standings(season = 2025, league_id = "103,104") |>
  transmute(
    team_id = team_records_team_id,
    w = team_records_wins,
    l = team_records_losses,
    rs = team_records_runs_scored,
    ra = team_records_runs_allowed,
    run_diff = team_records_run_differential
  )
stopifnot(identical(class(mlb_clubs$team_id), class(mlb_standings$team_id))) # same key type on both sides

mlb <- inner_join(mlb_clubs, mlb_standings, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(
    division = sub("^American League", "AL", sub("^National League", "NL", division)),
    color = sdv_team_colors("mlb", team)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(run_diff))
stopifnot(nrow(mlb) == 30)
```

```{r mlb-icons}
reactable(
  select(mlb, team, division, w, l, rs, ra, run_diff, color),
  defaultPageSize = 10,
  columns = list(
    team = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "mlb", height = 26), html = TRUE, width = 60),
    division = colDef(name = "Division", cell = pill_buttons(mlb, color_ref = "color", opacity = 0.85), minWidth = 110),
    w = colDef(name = "W", width = 55),
    l = colDef(name = "L", width = 55),
    rs = colDef(name = "RS", width = 60),
    ra = colDef(name = "RA", width = 60),
    run_diff = colDef(
      name = "Run diff",
      cell = icon_sets(mlb, icons = c("arrow-down", "minus", "arrow-up"), colors = c("#d7301f", "grey60", "#1a9850")),
      minWidth = 100
    ),
    color = colDef(show = FALSE)
  )
)
```

## 5. MLB: compare a team's logo variants with `embed_img()`

`embed_img()` draws a column that already holds image URLs. `sdv_logo_url()`
returns the URL of any variant `sdv_marks()` lists, so one table can set a
team's variants side by side, for picking the right one for a dark slide or a
scoreboard graphic. The dark variants sit on a dark cell background, where
they are meant to be read.

```{r mlb-variants}
variants <- mlb |>
  slice_head(n = 8) |>
  transmute(
    team,
    default = sdv_logo_url(team, league = "mlb"),
    cap = sdv_logo_url(team, league = "mlb", variant = "cap_on_light"),
    dark = sdv_logo_url(team, league = "mlb", variant = "dark"),
    cap_dark = sdv_logo_url(team, league = "mlb", variant = "cap_on_dark")
  )

on_dark <- list(background = "#1d1d1f")
reactable(
  variants,
  pagination = FALSE,
  defaultColDef = colDef(align = "center", width = 110),
  columns = list(
    team = colDef(name = "Team", width = 70),
    default = colDef(name = "Default", cell = embed_img(height = 44)),
    cap = colDef(name = "Cap", cell = embed_img(height = 44)),
    dark = colDef(name = "Dark", cell = embed_img(height = 44), style = on_dark),
    cap_dark = colDef(name = "Cap on dark", cell = embed_img(height = 44), style = on_dark)
  )
)
```

`embed_img()` writes no `alt` text and has no fallback when a URL is missing;
the `reactable_sdv_logos()` helper does both, so use `embed_img()` for this
kind of side-by-side review and the sdvplotR helper in tables readers see.

## 6. College football: a leaderboard with a reactablefmtr theme

reactablefmtr ships whole-table themes: `espn()`, `nytimes()`,
`fivethirtyeight()`, `pff()` and more. One `theme =` argument sets the fonts,
borders, header and hover styles. This one ranks the 25 FBS teams with the
best scoring margin, from ESPN's schedule data in cfbfastR's release files
(no API key). ESPN team ids go straight to `reactable_sdv_logos()`, and
`reactable_sdv_team_color_bar()` draws the margin bar in each team's color.

```{r cfb-data}
cfb_games <- cfbfastR::load_espn_cfb_schedules(2025) |>
  filter(season_type == 2, !is.na(home_score), !is.na(away_score))

cfb_side <- function(g, side, other) {
  transmute(g,
    team_id = as.character(.data[[paste0(side, "_id")]]),
    team = .data[[paste0(side, "_team")]],
    pts = .data[[paste0(side, "_score")]],
    opp = .data[[paste0(other, "_score")]]
  )
}
fbs <- sdv_teams("cfb")$team_id # sdvplotR's FBS and FCS programs, by ESPN id

cfb <- bind_rows(cfb_side(cfb_games, "home", "away"), cfb_side(cfb_games, "away", "home")) |>
  group_by(team_id, team) |>
  summarise(g = n(), w = sum(pts > opp), l = sum(pts < opp), margin = mean(pts - opp), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(g >= 10, team_id %in% fbs) |>
  arrange(desc(margin)) |>
  slice_head(n = 25) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), logo = team_id, .before = 1)
```

```{r cfb-theme}
reactable(
  select(cfb, rank, logo, team, w, l, margin),
  theme = espn(),
  defaultPageSize = 25,
  columns = list(
    rank = colDef(name = "#", width = 45),
    logo = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "cfb", height = 26), html = TRUE, width = 50),
    team = colDef(name = "Team", minWidth = 140),
    w = colDef(name = "W", width = 50),
    l = colDef(name = "L", width = 50),
    margin = colDef(
      name = "Margin per game", minWidth = 150,
      format = colFormat(digits = 1),
      style = reactable_sdv_team_color_bar(cfb, "team_id", league = "cfb")
    )
  )
)
```

Swap `espn()` for `nytimes()` or `fivethirtyeight()` and the same table takes
that site's look.

## 7. NFL: wordmarks with `reactable_sdv_wordmarks()`

A wordmark is the team's name as it is lettered on the uniform and the
stadium. `reactable_sdv_wordmarks()` draws it from the same team key as
`reactable_sdv_logos()`, with the same `height`, `variant` and fallback rules.
Wordmarks are wide, so give the column room. Here it heads a division
standings table built from nflreadr's schedules.

```{r nfl-wordmarks}
nfl_teams <- nflreadr::load_teams() |> select(team = team_abbr, division = team_division)
nfl <- nflreadr::load_schedules(2025) |>
  filter(game_type == "REG", !is.na(result)) |>
  nflreadr::clean_homeaway() |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    w = sum(team_score > opponent_score),
    l = sum(team_score < opponent_score),
    t = sum(team_score == opponent_score),
    pf = sum(team_score), pa = sum(opponent_score),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(nfl_teams, by = "team") |>
  mutate(logo = team, wordmark = team) |>
  arrange(division, desc(w + t / 2), desc(pf - pa))
stopifnot(nrow(nfl) == 32)

reactable(
  filter(nfl, division %in% c("AFC North", "NFC West")) |> select(division, logo, wordmark, w, l, t, pf, pa),
  pagination = FALSE,
  columns = list(
    division = colDef(name = "Division", width = 100),
    logo = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "nfl", height = 30), html = TRUE, width = 56),
    wordmark = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_wordmarks(league = "nfl", height = 24), html = TRUE, minWidth = 170),
    w = colDef(name = "W", width = 50), l = colDef(name = "L", width = 50), t = colDef(name = "T", width = 50),
    pf = colDef(name = "PF", width = 60), pa = colDef(name = "PA", width = 60)
  )
)
```

Logos in the column headers suit a head-to-head grid: `reactable_sdv_cols_label()`
turns every column named for a team into a logo header. Each cell is the row
team's point margin against the column team, summed over their two division
games.

```{r nfl-h2h}
nfc_west <- c("LA", "SEA", "SF", "ARI")
h2h <- nflreadr::load_schedules(2025) |>
  filter(game_type == "REG", !is.na(result)) |>
  nflreadr::clean_homeaway() |>
  filter(team %in% nfc_west, opponent %in% nfc_west) |>
  group_by(team, opponent) |>
  summarise(margin = sum(team_score - opponent_score), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = opponent, values_from = margin) |>
  select(team, all_of(nfc_west)) |>
  slice(match(nfc_west, team))

reactable(
  h2h,
  columns = c(
    list(team = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "nfl", height = 30), html = TRUE, width = 60)),
    reactable_sdv_cols_label(select(h2h, -team), league = "nfl", height = 30, align = "center", na = "")
  )
)
```

## 8. Men's college basketball: teams grouped by conference

`groupBy` folds the rows into one row per value of a column, and each column's
`aggregate` says how to summarise a group: `"mean"`, `"max"`, `"count"` and
others. Click a conference to open its teams. The ratings are hoopR's adjusted
efficiency margins for the 2025-26 season; each team's conference is the one
ESPN's standings list for that season, and the join keeps the Division I teams
(the ratings also hold the lower-division teams they played once). hoopR stores the ratings' team id as
text and the standings' as a number, so both are made text before the join.

```{r mbb-data}
mbb_ratings <- hoopR::load_mbb_ratings(2026) |>
  filter(season == 2026) |>
  transmute(team_id = as.character(team_id), adj_o, adj_d, adj_em)

mbb_conf <- hoopR::load_mbb_standings(2026) |>
  # ESPN also lists the College Basketball Crown, a postseason event, as a group
  filter(group_short_name != "CBC") |>
  distinct(team_id = as.character(team_id), team = team_short_display_name, conference = group_short_name)
stopifnot(identical(class(mbb_ratings$team_id), class(mbb_conf$team_id)), !anyDuplicated(mbb_conf$team_id))

mbb <- inner_join(mbb_conf, mbb_ratings, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(logo = team_id) |>
  arrange(desc(adj_em))
```

```{r mbb-groups}
reactable(
  select(mbb, conference, logo, team, adj_o, adj_d, adj_em),
  groupBy = "conference",
  defaultSorted = list(adj_em = "desc"),
  defaultPageSize = 12,
  columns = list(
    conference = colDef(name = "Conference", minWidth = 130),
    logo = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "mbb", height = 24), html = TRUE, width = 50),
    team = colDef(name = "Teams", aggregate = "count", minWidth = 120),
    adj_o = colDef(name = "Adj. off.", aggregate = "mean", format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    adj_d = colDef(name = "Adj. def.", aggregate = "mean", format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    adj_em = colDef(name = "Adj. margin", aggregate = "mean", format = colFormat(digits = 1))
  )
)
```

Sorting by the adjusted margin sorts the conferences by their teams' mean, so
the strongest conference is on top before any group is opened.

## 9. Conference logos in cells

sdvplotR keeps the college conferences' marks beside the teams', and the logo
helpers resolve a conference by its short name, full name or abbreviation
(`"Big East"`, `"Big East Conference"`). `sdv_teams("mbb", include_conferences = TRUE)`
lists them. This table is one row per conference, with the conference's logo
and the logo of its highest-rated team.

```{r mbb-conferences}
conferences <- mbb |>
  group_by(conference) |>
  summarise(
    teams = n(),
    mean_em = mean(adj_em),
    best = logo[which.max(adj_em)],
    best_em = max(adj_em),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(conf_logo = conference, .before = 1) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_em))

reactable(
  conferences,
  defaultPageSize = 12,
  columns = list(
    conf_logo = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "mbb", height = 30), html = TRUE, width = 60),
    conference = colDef(name = "Conference", minWidth = 120),
    teams = colDef(name = "Teams", width = 70),
    mean_em = colDef(name = "Mean adj. margin", format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    best = colDef(name = "Best team", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "mbb", height = 28), html = TRUE, align = "center"),
    best_em = colDef(name = "Its margin", format = colFormat(digits = 1))
  )
)
```

## 10. NBA: expand a team to its players

`details` takes a function of the row index and returns what to show when the
row is opened, here a second reactable of that team's eight players with the
most minutes, with ESPN headshots from `reactable_sdv_headshots()`. Only the
240 player rows travel with the page; the inner tables are built from them.

```{r nba-details}
nba_players <- hoopR::load_nba_player_box(2026) |>
  filter(season_type == 2, !did_not_play, !is.na(minutes), team_abbreviation %in% nba$team) |>
  group_by(team = team_abbreviation, athlete_id, player = athlete_display_name) |>
  summarise(g = n(), min = mean(minutes), pts = mean(points), reb = mean(rebounds), ast = mean(assists), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(team) |>
  slice_max(g * min, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

players_of <- function(abbr) {
  p <- filter(nba_players, team == abbr) |> select(athlete_id, player, g, min, pts, reb, ast)
  reactable(
    p,
    outlined = TRUE,
    defaultColDef = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 1), width = 60),
    columns = list(
      athlete_id = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_headshots(league = "nba", height = 36), html = TRUE, width = 56),
      player = colDef(name = "Player", minWidth = 150, width = NULL),
      g = colDef(name = "G", format = colFormat(digits = 0))
    )
  )
}

reactable(
  select(nba, team, wins, ppg, opp_ppg, margin),
  defaultPageSize = 10,
  details = function(index) players_of(nba$team[index]),
  columns = list(
    team = colDef(name = "", cell = reactable_sdv_logos(league = "nba", height = 28), html = TRUE, width = 60),
    wins = colDef(name = "W"),
    ppg = colDef(name = "PPG", format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    opp_ppg = colDef(name = "Opp PPG", format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    margin = colDef(name = "Margin", format = colFormat(digits = 1), style = reactable_sdv_team_color_bg(nba, "team", league = "nba"))
  )
)
```

## 11. A static version for a post

A reactable is HTML, so it does not go into a slide or a social post as it is.
The first recipe's numbers draw as a ggplot with the same team colors:
`geom_col()` takes each team's color with `scale_fill_identity()`, and
`geom_sdv_logos()` puts the logo at the end of each bar.

```{r export, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Horizontal bar chart of the 30 NBA teams' average point margin per game in the 2025-26 regular season, each bar in the team's primary color with its logo at the bar's end, sorted from the best margin at the top to the worst at the bottom."}
ggplot(nba, aes(margin, reorder(team, margin))) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = color), width = 0.7) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team, x = margin + sign(margin) * 0.9), league = "nba", height = 0.028) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.08)) +
  labs(
    title = "NBA point margin per game, 2025-26 regular season",
    x = "Points scored minus points allowed, per game", y = NULL,
    caption = "Data: ESPN via hoopR  |  Chart: sdvplotR"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

BibTeX Citation

```bibtex
@misc{gilani_carl_lee_kay_weatherman_sdvplotR,
  author = {Gilani, Saiem and Carl, Sebastian and Lee, Jared and Kay, Camden and Weatherman, Andrew},
  title = {sdvplotR: The SportsDataverse's R Package for Multi-League Sports Plotting.},
  url = {https://sdvplotR.sportsdataverse.org},
  year = {2026}
}
```
